facts.text: Hanford was founded in 1909, annexed by Columbus in 1955, marketed to African American veterans, but much was lost when I‑70 was built in the 1960s.
The Lincoln Theater, a historic jazz venue, has been carefully restored and is a centerpiece of the area's African American cultural heritage.
Bryden Road showcases more than 50 architectural styles, from French and German to Renaissance influences, reflecting the neighborhood's diverse history.
The neighborhood has shifted from historic landmarks to new businesses and residential developments, illustrating its ongoing revitalization.
Hanford Village earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places, preserving its early 20th‑century character.
The area received historic neighborhood status in 1986, formalizing its cultural and architectural significance.
